google.title: Mental health therapy in Hampshire, Whiteley | Re;mind
google.description: Mental health therapy in Hampshire at Re;mind, Whiteley: counselling, EMDR, hypnotherapy, VR therapy and coaching, in person or online. Rated 4.8 on Google.

notes.title: How the page appears on Google
notes.text: The blue title and the short description are written by us, and the search phrase comes first in both. Most people decide from these two lines alone. The homepage keeps the short web address remindmht.com, the front door to every other page.

notes.title: The main headline
notes.text: It asks the question people type and answers it in the same breath: “Looking for mental health therapy in Hampshire? Re;mind, shaped around you”. It is the first thing anyone who lands here reads, and it tells Google plainly what the page is about.

notes.title: The opening answer
notes.text: Four short sentences answer straight away: where, with whom, for what, and how it feels. This is the part Google and AI assistants such as ChatGPT are most likely to quote.

notes.title: The search phrase in the section headings
notes.text: The first heading under the headline asks “Where can I get mental health therapy in Hampshire?” and the lines beneath answer it. The same words come back in five more of the main headings, each time inside a real question, which is how Google confirms what the page is about.

notes.title: The picture description
notes.text: Every photograph carries a short written description that Google reads and that a screen reader speaks aloud. This one carries the search phrase as well.

notes.title: Real Google reviews, word for word
notes.text: Three of your 20 Google reviews are quoted exactly as written, with each reviewer’s first name and initial, beside the facts that matter: a clinical psychologist on the team, seven days a week, free parking. Real reviews are among the strongest signs of trust a visitor can see, and the star rating links to all 20 on Google, so nothing is hidden.

notes.title: Named people stand behind the page
notes.text: Five named therapists with their roles, and at the foot of the page: written by Susie Deacon, clinically reviewed by Dr Jane Gilbert, Doctor of Clinical Psychology, with the date it was last updated. Google is careful with health pages and favours ones that a real, qualified person stands behind.

notes.title: Clear fees and practical details
notes.text: Fees, session length, payment, where you are and who you see, all in one place. People who find these answers tend to get in touch rather than move on. Anything in square brackets is our best guess for you to confirm.

notes.title: Questions and answers
notes.text: Five questions people ask before they start, each answered in a few plain sentences. Clear questions with short answers are exactly what Google and AI assistants look for when someone asks a question.

notes.title: Ways to get in touch
notes.text: The form sits at the top of the page and again at the bottom, next to the three plain steps to starting, and your phone number is in the top bar of every page. Nobody has to hunt for it.

notes.title: Links between the pages
notes.text: The VR therapy row leads to the VR therapy page, Claire’s example story on this page leads to the full case study, and both of those pages link back here. Google follows these links to see how the pages belong together, and visitors use them to find the help they came for.

notes.title: Working quietly in the background
notes.text: Behind the scenes, the page carries labels that tell Google what it is: a therapy practice in Whiteley, with its address, opening hours and phone number in a form Google reads directly. The page also loads quickly on a phone and works for people who use a screen reader or larger text.
